rundown: Heat beat Knicks 108-105 at Madison Square Garden in New York, NY in front of 19,812. Heat led 60-44 at the half and held on. The 1st quarter decided it: Heat won it 31-21.
Leading the way — Heat: Bam Adebayo 25 pts; Davion Mitchell 9 ast; Giannis Antetokounmpo 23 reb. Knicks: Jalen Brunson 27 pts, 8 ast; Karl-Anthony Towns 10 reb.
Where Heat won it: they won the boards 43-42 and turned it over 9 times to 16.

Against the closing line (DraftKings): Knicks closed as 2.5-point favorites and lost outright to Heat; Heat won as the underdog at +124; the total closed at 221.5 and they combined for 213, under by 8.5.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 27, 6:52 PM ET. It had Heat 25% and Knicks 75%, projecting Heat 108 – Knicks 116 (223.9 total, Knicks by 8).

Final: Heat 108 – Knicks 105. Wrong winner: it had Knicks at 75%, and Heat (25%) won.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Heat came in with a 4% above average attack and a 2% leakier than average defense (10-7, 119.7 scored and 118.9 allowed a game over 17 games), worth about 103 and 103 games of evidence. Projected to score 108, they scored 108 (+0 points, 0% over); projected to allow 116, they allowed 105 (−11 points, 9% under).

Knicks came in with a league-average attack and a 5% stingier than average defense (12-6, 109.6 scored and 103.2 allowed a game over 18 games), worth about 111 and 110 games of evidence. Projected to score 116, they scored 105 (−11 points, 9% under); projected to allow 108, they allowed 108 (+0 points, 0% over).

The bigger miss was Knicks' scoring (-11 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 213 against 223.9 projected (-10.9), about the 27th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±18.2).

Margin: Heat by 3 against Knicks by 8 projected, about the 18th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±12).

An ordinary result: inside the range the simulations expected most of the time.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Market (Line movement signal): Knicks ×1.02, Heat ×1.00. It favored Knicks, who did not beat their projection by more than the other side did.

review.title: Against the market
review.body:
NY ML (-148) at -148: the algo gave it 59% vs 57% fair (+1.7 pts) — lost (-1u); lost to the close (closing fair chance 57%). MIA ML (+124) at +124: the algo gave it 41% vs 43% fair (-1.7 pts) — won (+1.2u); lost to the close (closing fair chance 43%). NY -2.5 (-112) at -112: the algo gave it 52% vs 50% fair (+1.6 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close. MIA +2.5 (-108) at -108: the algo gave it 48% vs 50% fair (-1.6 pts) — won (+0.9u); same number as the close. OVER 221.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 50% vs 50% fair (+0.5 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close. UNDER 221.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 50% vs 50% fair (-0.5 pts) — won (+0.9u); same number as the close.

The line barely moved between the algo's snapshot and the close.

No bet: nothing cleared the algo's bar before the game.

review.title: Where the public and the money were
review.body:
Splits (Action Network): spread: 53% of bets on Heat, 59% of the money — Heat covered; total: 80% of bets on the over, 75% of the money — it went under; moneyline: 29% of bets on Heat, 27% of the money.

The sharp side by the algo's read was Knicks, who lost and didn't cover.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.943 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by -10.9 points. It counts toward NBA scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 164 graded NBA games the algo now scales scoring ×0.991 and gives home teams +0.1 points. Team corrections so far: Heat attack ×1.011, defense ×0.994 (11 games); Knicks attack ×0.987, defense ×0.973 (12 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Wrong side, total within its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
